investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod ever reached a running state, the eval runner never obtained a VM ID or a remote state value, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing a complete contract validation failure.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for peer-pod VMs at the time of the eval run. Preemption was also exhausted ("No preemption victims found for incoming pod"). The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1885 calls createAgent with machineType "remote", which triggers the pod submission that stalls; because the pod never becomes ready, the runner never writes vmIdPresent, remoteState, agentId, or orgId into the evidence object, violating the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:256-259. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. All three sibling checks hit the same error within the same ~7-minute window, indicating the resource was not freed between attempts.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remaining 4 nodes are structurally ineligible for peer-pod scheduling regardless of resource availability, reducing effective capacity to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are at their VM slot limit, the cluster has zero schedulable headroom.

Tertiary — leaked or stuck remote-agent VMs from prior eval runs or user workloads consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if previous agent pods were not cleaned up (e.g., withCleanup at run-status-probes.mjs:1883 failed silently on a prior run), those slots would remain occupied.

Lower confidence — transient cluster event (node drain, maintenance, or scale-down) that temporarily removed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity: no node event or incident signal is present in the supplied evidence, so this cannot be confirmed or ruled out from the packet alone.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-14T18:43–18:48Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule new kata peer-pod VMs because 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that carry the peer-pod runtime. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to schedule a new remote-agent pod times out (~139–144 s), preventing agent creation and all downstream state polling. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; the impact is scoped to the observability eval suite for the remote-agents feature.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two peer-pod-capable nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agents or leaked pods, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests. Supported directly by failed-check.message and all three sibling check messages.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-peer-pod nodes are excluded by the pod spec's affinity rules, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 peer-pod nodes. If those rules changed or nodes were relabeled, effective capacity would drop to zero even with partial VM quota remaining.

TERTIARY — Leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, preventing new pods from being scheduled. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is intended to release resources, but a prior crash or timeout could leave orphaned pods.

LOWER — Cluster node count reduction: if the two peer-pod nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or removed, the effective kata.peerpods.io/vm pool would shrink to zero without a quota configuration change.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod ever reached a running state, the eval runner never obtained a VM ID or a remote state value, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing a complete contract validation failure.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for peer-pod VMs at the time of the eval run. Preemption was also exhausted ("No preemption victims found for incoming pod"). The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1885 calls createAgent with machineType "remote", which triggers the pod submission that stalls; because the pod never becomes ready, the runner never writes vmIdPresent, remoteState, agentId, or orgId into the evidence object, violating the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:256-259. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler verdict 'pod stuck unscheduled for 139s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=144568, status=fail — pod timed out well before the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000ms but exceeded the warningLatencyMs of 240000ms; the pod was stuck for ~139s before the check gave up.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written, confirming the agent pod never reached a schedulable state.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields [orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState] are missing, matching the empty evidence object.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), latencyMs=150582, evidenceKeys=[] — confirms the capacity exhaustion persisted across a second independent pod submission.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=150352, evidenceKeys=[] — confirms the capacity exhaustion persisted across a third independent pod submission.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which is the code path that submits the pod requiring kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. All three sibling checks hit the same error within the same ~7-minute window, indicating the resource was not freed between attempts.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remaining 4 nodes are structurally ineligible for peer-pod scheduling regardless of resource availability, reducing effective capacity to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are at their VM slot limit, the cluster has zero schedulable headroom.

Tertiary — leaked or stuck remote-agent VMs from prior eval runs or user workloads consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if previous agent pods were not cleaned up (e.g., withCleanup at run-status-probes.mjs:1883 failed silently on a prior run), those slots would remain occupied.

Lower confidence — transient cluster event (node drain, maintenance, or scale-down) that temporarily removed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity: no node event or incident signal is present in the supplied evidence, so this cannot be confirmed or ruled out from the packet alone.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-14T18:43–18:48Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule new kata peer-pod VMs because 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that carry the peer-pod runtime. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to schedule a new remote-agent pod times out (~139–144 s), preventing agent creation and all downstream state polling. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; the impact is scoped to the observability eval suite for the remote-agents feature.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-14T18:43–18:48Z because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to help. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner could not create a remote agent, and consequently no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was ever produced, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector requirements. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~139–144 seconds before the eval timed out. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion or misconfiguration failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling path, not an eval infrastructure or code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet; the impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval for the remote-agents feature.

possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the extended VM resource pool is fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no allocatable capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures.

[High confidence] Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or label drift on 4 of 6 nodes: the pod spec requires a node label or affinity rule that only 2 nodes carry (the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes), and those 2 are already saturated. If the affinity rule is overly restrictive or node labels were removed, scheduling would fail even with available VM slots.

[Medium confidence] Cluster under-provisioning for peak load: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes may have insufficient total VM quota to serve concurrent eval and production workloads simultaneously, causing resource starvation during the eval window.
[Low confidence] Transient spike in remote-agent workload consuming all VM slots just before the eval ran, with no preemption victims available to reclaim capacity.

Verify whether the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes are intentionally excluded from remote-agent scheduling or whether label drift has reduced the eligible node pool unexpectedly. If label drift occurred, restore the correct labels.

Review the node affinity/selector rules in the remote-agent pod spec to confirm they are as restrictive as intended and that the eligible node count is sufficient for concurrent eval and production workloads.

Consider adding a cluster-level alert on kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization approaching 100% on eligible nodes so capacity exhaustion is detected before it causes eval or workload failures.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes shows available (unallocated) VM capacity at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint must be investigated.

If the remote-agent pod spec does not actually request kata.peerpods.io/vm as an extended resource, the 'Insufficient' message would indicate a scheduler bug or label conflict rather than true resource exhaustion.

If a subsequent eval run (with no other changes) succeeds and produces all 5 required evidence keys, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief workload spike) rather than a persistent capacity problem.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in the same run window, the root cause would be isolated to the runtime probe's pod spec rather than shared cluster capacity.

If the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes are found to carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm label with available capacity, the node affinity/selector in the pod spec is the primary defect rather than resource exhaustion on the 2 currently eligible nodes.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity directly (e.g., checks allocatable vs. allocated ratio) and alerts before the pool reaches exhaustion, decoupled from the full agent lifecycle eval.

Add a node-label integrity eval that verifies the expected number of nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm label, alerting on pool shrinkage due to label drift or node loss.
